QUIET LUXURY, OBVIOUS CONTROLS

The two ideas are the same idea. Expensive design is restraint — one action per screen, a lot of space around it, a serif reserved for the four numbers that matter. That restraint is also what makes it easy: there is only ever one thing to press.

Bone paper, ink, a deep green for anything confirmed, brass for level and milestones. Nothing gold, nothing loud. Every screen here is live.

THE CORE LOOP

Find a game → see who is playing and how even the sides are → release your place and get your money back → say who played well.

Start with screen 3. Tap "I can't make it", then "Offer my place", and watch what happens. That single interaction is the whole competitive argument.

WHY THESE THREE

Neither CeleBreak nor Stranger Soccer has any of it. The member card makes your standing portable between cities, the season makes next Thursday matter, and hosting turns the organisers they compete with into supply.

THE RULES THAT MAKE IT LUXURIOUS

One serif, used about four times a screen. One action, 58px, pill, at the bottom. One dark surface, spent on exactly three moments — the scoreline, the member card, the refund.

If everything is a moment, nothing is. Most of the craft here is in what was left out.
